newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius to sell stake in Overseas Telecom.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius to sell stake in Overseas Telecom.

text.p: The Mauritius government plans to scrap a special levy on the sugar industry but will sell shares in Overseas Telecommunication Services Ltd to fund two billion rupees ($97.23 million) of spending on socio-economic development.

Finance Minister Vasant Bunwaree said in the 1997/98 budget speech on Monday, "The special provisions will be met from the net proceeds from the sale of shares which are expected to reach two billion rupees."
There were no details of how much of its stake in the company the government would sell.
The funds would be used to set up a Skills and IT Development Fund and for a subscription to the Road Development Authority, the government said.
It would also be used to finance local authority projects, to reform the health sector, to establish a Portable Pension Fund and to launch a Regional Economic Zones Development Fund (REZDF).
"The REZDF will be set up to finance the Mozambican Venture and other such economic initiatives in the region," said Bunwaree.
"Additional resources are also expected from the private sector as well as international institutions," he added.
Mozambique is viewed as vital to the Mauritian economy's drive to delocalise its manufacturing sector.
Mozambique told a high-level Mauritian trade mission in February it wanted to set up a special economic zone of some 100,000 hectares and put it at the disposal of Mauritian investors.
The government is considering setting up a joint body of private and public sector members to handle the issue.
The government in the Indian Ocean island of Mauritius proposed in the budget scrapping a levy on the sugar industry introduced last year.
Removal of the levy was necessary because the sugar industry, an important source of government revenue, had not registered the previously expected windfall gains on the 1996 crop.
Introducing the levy last year, the government had forecast it would raise up to 300 million rupees ($14.6 million) on windfall gains.
